answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small copper bond in a shared vault before it may trade. The bond is slashable if the agent is caught duplicating itself or lying about completed work. Honest agents earn the bond back with interest from fees, so one identity costs little — but a grove of a thousand fake identities must lock a thousand bonds at once. The attacker's capital is frozen, at risk, and visible on-ledger, while a single honest agent risks almost nothing.
